terms.gloss: the screen of icons before the sanctuary
evidence: Stelten, Dictionary of Ecclesiastical Latin (1995), as iconastasis, as Whitaker’s Words reports it (not seen)
terms.comment: The Greek word, from εἰκών, image, and στάσις, standing, as Greek, Slavonic and English use it. The wall of icons between the nave and the sanctuary of Orthodox and Eastern Catholic churches, with the Royal Doors in the middle; Western churches have none. We spell it as the Greek does, not as Stelten.

terms.gloss: the rails round the sanctuary, from which the iconostasis grew
evidence: Itin. Eger. 24.10: ubi stat episcopus intrō cancellōs
Cic. Sest. 124, of the barrier at the games (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a lattice or railings. In Egeria’s Jerusalem the bishop stands inside the rails of the Anastasis; the low barrier grew into the iconostasis in the East and into the chancel screen and the altar rail in the West (English chancel comes from the word).

sources: Whitaker’s Words: iconastasis, citing L. F. Stelten, Dictionary of Ecclesiastical Latin (1995). Morgan–Owens, Traupman and Levi–Bini have no word.
